skill.name: generate-output
skill.description: Generate complete code, documentation, tests, refactors, or content from validated requirements while following saved project standards.
skill.summary: Create ready-to-use deliverables from validated requirements and project standards.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 81 opens a Markdown javascript code fence and the block shows a StandardsRepository usage example. It does not invoke a shell or execute user-controlled commands.

The backticks on line 93 format a local documentation path in Markdown. Referencing `.claude/lib/standards-repository.md` is not command execution.

content.value_statement: Teams often have validated requirements but still need polished final output. This skill turns those requirements into ready-to-use code, documentation, tests, refactors, or content.
actual_capabilities: Generates code, documentation, tests, refactors, or written content from validated requirements.
Loads project type standards and applies saved principles when available.
Falls back to best practices when no saved standards exist.
Structures output with a summary, applied principles, common patterns, deliverable, and next steps.
Includes supporting elements such as examples, comments, tests, or troubleshooting guidance when relevant.
limitations: It assumes requirements were validated before use.
It references a StandardsRepository interface that is not included in this skill package.
It does not execute generated code or run tests.
Output quality depends on the clarity of requirements and saved standards.

use_cases.title: Build a Feature Deliverable
use_cases.description: Create production-ready feature code with typing, error handling, examples, and project-specific conventions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn approved requirements into structured documentation with examples, use cases, and troubleshooting notes.

use_cases.title: Create a Test Suite
use_cases.description: Generate maintainable tests that cover happy paths, edge cases, setup, teardown, and naming conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Deliverable
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after requirements are approved.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use generate-output to create a [deliverable type] from these validated requirements: [requirements]. Project type: [project type].

prompt_templates.title: Apply Saved Standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Use project conventions when standards are available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the final deliverable for [project type]. Apply these saved principles and common patterns: [standards]. Requirements: [requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Produce Code With Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate a feature package with supporting validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate production-ready code for [feature]. Include type annotations, error handling, usage notes, and tests for edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Full Release Artifact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a polished multi-section output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the complete release deliverable for [initiative]. Include summary, principles applied, patterns included, final output, and next steps.

output_examples.input: Validated requirements for a searchable dropdown component with keyboard navigation.
output: A complete React component plan with TypeScript expectations.
Coverage notes for keyboard behavior, error states, and usage examples.
A next steps section for testing and review.

output_examples.input: Approved request to document a new onboarding workflow.
output: A structured guide with overview, steps, examples, and troubleshooting.
A summary of standards applied from the project documentation rules.

output_examples.input: Validated refactor request for a duplicated service layer.
output: A before and after explanation of the refactor.
A description of behavioral changes and quality improvements.

best_practices: Run this skill only after requirements are validated and complete.
Provide the project type and any saved standards before generation.
Review generated output with real project tests and human judgment.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to replace requirements discovery or validation.
Do not accept generated code without checking behavior and security.
Do not omit project standards when they are available.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after requirements are validated and you need the final deliverable created.

faq.question: What types of output can it create?
faq.answer: It can create code, documentation, refactors, tests, and structured written content.

faq.question: Does it validate requirements?
faq.answer: No. It expects requirements to be reviewed before the skill runs.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It can write test content, but it does not execute the tests.

faq.question: How does it use project standards?
faq.answer: It reads available standards and applies saved principles, patterns, and conventions to the output.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
